rea.capabilityFinding: REA JavaScript/Electron analysis is appropriate for authorized local application artifacts; it is not a universal URL/repository auditor. Use source inspection, official docs and tests for Rust projects, protocol docs and API services.
rea.limitations: Prior local analysis is structural evidence only; no claim of runtime loading, semantic equivalence, upstream behavior, provider correctness, or economic advantage.

provenance: Local SYLPH Jito status adapters and live-status report
discoveries: A successful sendBundle response with bundle_id means receipt, not landing; the documented status method must be used to observe bundle processing.
Jito bundles are atomic and all-or-nothing within a slot, while tip amount participates in an auction and a low tip may fail selection.

Inflight bundle status is retained for only five minutes; Invalid or null/empty results mean no status is retained in that window, not relay failure or proof of non-landing. The local coordinator now reports STATUS_NOT_RETAINED as nonterminal and leaves chain reconciliation authoritative.
patterns: separate submission receipt from landing/finalization evidence
correlate bundle IDs to transaction signatures and settlement
treat expired/missing inflight status as unresolved and reconcile finalized chain state
measure tip, priority fees, base fees, retries and failed/uncled outcomes
convert decimal SOL tip-floor observations to lamports with exact integer ceiling and clamp to the configured maximum
sources.overlap: SYLPH has read-only Block Engine connectivity and tip-floor research projections. The Jito lifecycle coordinator now distinguishes missing/expired inflight status from relay failure, while finalized chain reconciliation remains authoritative. The tip-floor parser converts the API's decimal SOL value to lamports using integer arithmetic and clamps to the configured maximum. Bundle submission and realized landed-cost telemetry remain unverified.

tips and priority fees can exceed expected edge
bundle execution differs from ordinary transaction submission
validation: only in isolated fixtures or explicitly authorized non-capital environment
test receipt-without-landing and status timeout
test Invalid, null and empty inflight results as nonterminal status-not-retained outcomes

provenance: Official Jupiter Developer docs index and Swap API V2 reference, fetched 2026-10-15
Official Jupiter RTSE and transaction-version documentation
Current official Jupiter Build and Transaction Versions docs fetched 2026-10-15
Local V0-only response guard and deterministic Jupiter V2 build regression
discoveries: Swap API V2 recommends /order plus /execute for managed execution and /build for custom instruction composition; /execute is unavailable for /build transactions. SYLPH keeps its /order research adapter quote-only and its /build result as INSTRUCTIONS_ONLY.

The current /build response identifies V0/V1 modes. V1 has no compute-budget instructions or ALTs and returns computeUnitPrice for message config; V0 returns a compute-unit price instruction but no compute-unit limit. Jupiter recommends simulating the assembled transaction, then using 1.2x consumed units capped at 1.4M.

The current /build response identifies transactionVersion as 0 or 1; V1 has no compute-budget instructions or ALTs and instead returns computeUnitPrice for the message config. A client that does not explicitly request and validate the response version can misclassify a V1 build as V0.
patterns: keep quote-only response schemas distinct from prepared transaction schemas
validate mint and raw token amounts against their integer width before arithmetic
record quote timestamps and sequential round-trip window
preserve fixed slippage guardrails for the configured V0 build path
treat V1 message-config compute budgets as a separate compatibility implementation before requesting transactionVersion=1
simulate the complete instruction set with resolved ALTs before choosing the compute limit; derive the fee from the returned micro-lamport price and selected limit
sources.overlap: SYLPH previously relied on Jupiter’s default V0 response but did not send transactionVersion=0 or validate the response transactionVersion. It could therefore accept a V1 response through a V0-only instruction path, where V1 priority-fee configuration is carried outside the returned ComputeBudget instructions. The path now explicitly requests V0, requires response version 0 (number or canonical string), and records instructionTransactionVersion: 0 while leaving transactionVersion null because no serialized transaction is produced. It remains INSTRUCTIONS_ONLY and live signing/submission is quarantined. It now simulates the full V0 instruction set with response ALTs at a 1.4M-unit ceiling, rejects simulation errors or incomplete usage, inserts a 1.2x compute-unit limit capped at 1.4M, and computes the priority fee with integer ceiling from the V0 CU-price instruction and selected limit. The paper build uses this route-specific fee instead of the blanket configured maximum; route evidence emits amounts as decimal strings.
risks: V1 message config, V1 wallet signing, and V1 finalized transaction reconciliation remain unsupported.
Simulation is a provider/RPC snapshot and can differ from landing state; it does not prove quote fill, landing, or realized PnL.
No live Jupiter API or RPC simulation was run; integration evidence uses deterministic response and simulation fixtures.
validation: Explicitly request transactionVersion=0 and require response transactionVersion 0; reject missing, unknown, or V1 versions.
Simulate the assembled instructions and verified ALT state at the maximum CU limit; reject transaction errors, absent units, zero units, and usage outside the supported range.
Set the final limit to ceil(1.2 x simulated units), capped at 1.4M, and calculate priority fee from the exact V0 compute-unit price with integer ceiling.
Keep amount, output-threshold, signer, compute-fee-cap, and lookup-table checks passing; use confirmed fills for realized execution accounting.

provenance: Official Pump public documentation repository README
discoveries: Official docs describe new Pump curve v3 and PumpSwap v2 instruction families, multi-hop swaps, pump-token quote mints and fee sweeps; the lifecycle is broader than a SOL-only bonding curve followed by one AMM.

PumpSwap effective quote reserves are the quote-vault balance plus signed virtual_quote_reserves; docs explicitly warn the signed reserve may be negative and raw vault balance alone is not the quote reserve.

Fees can accrue on curves/pools and be swept separately; synthetic migration behavior and creator/holder-reward fee variants affect interpretation of trade events and quote/accounting state. The pinned PumpSwap SDK rounds LP, protocol and creator sell fees separately, so a combined-fee multiplication can produce a different net quote.
patterns: version account/instruction decoders
model quote mint and reserve signs explicitly
preserve raw and signed virtual reserves alongside effective reserves
round each protocol fee component as the venue SDK does and check real quote-vault sufficiency
separate trade events from fee-sweep events
bind pool/lifecycle state to slot and canonical account identity
surface bounded pool observation provenance and failure states in the operator position view
sources.overlap: Market supports native-SOL bonding-curve reads and quotes. The graduation bridge requires supplied pool venue, address, quote mint, reserves, fee and slot, and rejects AMM buys unless the observation is the exact immutable object produced by the canonical RPC reader; a caller cannot forge the source label. The PumpSwap reader derives the canonical SOL pool, refetches pool/mint/vault/global/fee accounts in one context, validates token-program ownership, expected associated-token addresses, pool-PDA token authority and vault mints, handles signed virtual quote reserves, and computes fees through the pinned PumpSwap SDK. Market calls it after curve completion and keeps migration pending on failure. Engine snapshots and the positions table surface observation state, slot, provenance, staleness and bounded error codes. The path is SOL-quote only; broader PumpSwap lifecycle, alternate quote conversion, route execution and a recovery certificate are not implemented.

non-SOL quote pools cannot be converted into SOL exit proceeds without an independently observed conversion quote
curve completion is not proof of destination-pool liquidity
fee sweeps and migration events can corrupt volume/PnL attribution if treated as trades
